title: Central Zoo Authority (CZA)
definition: A statutory body established under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, mandated to oversee, regulate, and provide technical/financial assistance to zoos across India to ensure high standards of animal welfare and conservation.
importanceInUpsc: Frequently tested in Environment Prelims regarding statutory status, composition, and its role in ex-situ conservation. Mains relevance lies in biodiversity management and animal welfare ethics.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Central Zoo Authority.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
